newsitem.title: USA: Atlas Air jumps after jet deal.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Air jumps after jet deal.

text.p: Shares of Atlas Air Inc jumped about 9.5 percent after the air cargo carrier said it agreed to purchase 10 Boeing Co jets, a move which is expected to improve operating costs.
Atlas said it will purchase 10 new Boeing 747-400 freighter aircraft, with the option to purchase an additional 10, the company said. Terms were not disclosed.
Atlas gained 2-7/8 to 31-5/8 in afternoon trading.

The 747-400s burn less fuel, have longer range and greater payload capability than the 747-200 jets in its fleet. Atlas will now be able to fly from Hong Kong to Europe with only one stop to refuel, versus two stops previously, analysts said.

The jets will serve as replacements for the five Federal Express Corp aircraft currently on lease through the end of this year, the company said. Analysts said the new jets will reduce routine maintenance and fuel costs.
Michael Shonstrom, an analyst with Neidiger Tucker Bruner, said the 747-400 is "an important plane" to serve the fast-growing demand for the high gross weight market.

"By investing in the 747-400, we are investing in a broader, more customer responsive fleet and positioning ourselves for an increasingly demanding marketplace. We believe that this acquisition will not only reduce Atlas' operating costs for the next decade, but it will also provide new aircraft for those markets where new aircraft are preferred," Atlas Air said in a prepared statement.
Scott & Stringfellow analyst Alex Brand said he upgraded Altas Air to strong buy from neutral.
"For me, this deal clears up a lot of business risk concerns. The long-term impact of this deal is just overwhelmingly positive and offsets any near-term risk," said Brand.
